the time-modulation of the number of EC--decay events in the GSI--experiment can be explained by a quantum mechanical interference of two different neutrino flavours.
the time-modulated orbital electron capture decay in an ion storage ring is explained by neutrino flavour mixing, which can be understood within quantum field theory.
the time--modulated EC decay in H--like $^{140}{Pr}$ is caused by neutrino--oscillations.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neutrino--flavor oscillations can be studied in the time-modulated orbital electron capture (EC).
the observed oscillations are a clear indication for a non-vanishing neutrino--flavor mixing and a finite neutrino mass.
the observed modulation in the EC-decay rate in an ion storage ring is a direct proof for the existence of neutrino--flavor mixing and for a finite neutrino mass difference.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to show that the time-modulation of the number of EC--daughter ions in the experiment can be explained by the neutrino--flavor mixing.
the neutrino--flavor mixing is not only an important phenomenon for astrophysics, but also for the atomic physics of the heavy ions.
the neutrino oscillation phenomenon is a general feature of quantum field theory and that the neutrino flavour mixing is a general feature in nature.
